body.statement: At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) satisfying the displayed rank conditions, profiling the \(J\)-coordinate map \(q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-D(x)\) over the unrestricted path of \(\delta_1^0(x)\) yields the observed normal \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}\) for \(-A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)\). Its displayed coordinates have Gram rank at most \(J-1\), and the rank is exactly \(J-1\) whenever \(E_{P_{0,O}}[R_{\mathrm{PT},x}R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}]\) has rank \(J-1\). For either branch, \(\mathcal T_b(P_0)=\{s\in\mathcal H_{P_0}:E_{P_{0,O}}[R_{b,x}s]=0\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X\}\) and \(\mathcal I_b(P_0)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{b,x}+\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}\). Consequently, \(\phi_b=\sum_x g_{b,x}-R_b^{\prime}\{E_{P_{0,O}}[R_bR_b^{\prime}]\}^{\dagger}E_{P_{0,O}}[R_b\sum_xg_{b,x}]\), with redundant PT and SC rows handled by the Moore--Penrose inverse.
body.justification: This gives the two branch faces in one observed-data Hilbert space and exposes the SC-weight derivative normals that a PT-only calculation omits.
body.gap: ChenSantAnnaXie2025, Theorem 3.1, derives the PT canonical gradient; SunXieZhang2025, Appendix equations (A.5) and (A.13), gives estimator-specific branch influence laws, but neither paper characterizes both affine influence classes at their intersection.
body.consumer: The normal-form representation is the input required to calculate an identification-robust standard error for the Alaska minimum-wage analysis in SunXieZhang2025.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(E_0\) for \(E_{P_{0,O}}\), and put \(G_b=\sum_xg_{b,x}\).  First consider PT.  Since \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\mathbf 1_J=0\), differentiation of
\[
 q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-D(x)
\]
after allowing an arbitrary derivative of the latent scalar \(\delta_1^0(x)\) gives
\[
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}\dot q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=-A_{\mathrm{PT}}\dot D(x).
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus the latent derivative has disappeared, and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\) says precisely that the Riesz representer of (1) is \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}\).  The symmetric idempotent matrix \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\) has null space \(\operatorname{span}(\mathbf 1_J)\), hence matrix rank \(J-1\).  Therefore the Gram rank of the displayed statistical representers is at most \(J-1\).  It is exactly \(J-1\) under the additional nondegeneracy condition stated in the corrected claim.  The qualification is necessary: if all donor outcomes are conditionally constant, the mean derivatives, and hence the corresponding Riesz representers, can vanish even though \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\) itself has matrix rank \(J-1\).

We next identify the observed tangent spaces rather than assuming them.  In the PT branch the observable restriction is \(r_{\mathrm{PT},x}=-A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)=0\).  Conversely, any observed law satisfying these equal-donor-change equations has a compatible PT full-data extension: conditionally on \((G=1,X=x)\), choose an unobserved \(Y_T(0)\) whose mean is \(\mu_{1,T-1}(x)+\Delta\mu_2(x)\), retain all observed coordinates, and impose the already assumed no-anticipation equalities before \(T\).  In the SC branch, full column rank of \(B(x)\) makes \(w(x)=\{B(x)'B(x)\}^{-1}B(x)'a(x)\) unique and smooth.  The equation \(r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=0\) is equivalent to \(a(x)=B(x)w(x)\).  Conversely, an observed law satisfying this equation has an SC full-data extension obtained by choosing the unobserved treated-group \(Y_T(0)\) to have conditional mean \(w(x)'(\mu_{2,T}(x),\ldots,\mu_{J+1,T}(x))'\).  Hence, locally, the observed projections of the two full-data branches are exactly the zero sets of their displayed finite moment maps.

For a score \(s\) of a branch submodel, differentiating \(r_{b,x}=0\) and using Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\) gives
\[
 E_0[R_{b,x}s]=0\quad\text{for every }x.
 \tag{2}
\]
For the reverse inclusion, retain a maximal independent row system of the derivative of \((r_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X)\).  The locally constant-rank hypothesis permits a nonsingular coordinate minor.  Given a bounded score in the kernel in (2), exponentially tilt the observed law by that score and by one bounded score for each retained row.  Solving the finitely many equations \(r_{b,x}=0\) for the latter coefficients uses that nonsingular minor; differentiating the equations at zero shows that all correction coefficients have derivative zero because (2) holds.  Thus the resulting restriction-preserving path has the prescribed score.  Truncating and recentering an arbitrary \(s\in L_0^2(P_{0,O})\), and applying the same finite-dimensional correction before taking the \(L^2\) limit, proves
\[
 \mathcal T_b(P_0)=\bigcap_{x\in\mathcal X}\ker\{s\mapsto E_0[R_{b,x}s]\}.
 \tag{3}
\]
The full-data extensions in the preceding paragraph show that these corrected observed paths are induced by paths in the required causal branch.

Because there are finitely many rows, (3) and elementary Hilbert-space duality give
\[
 \mathcal T_b(P_0)^\perp=\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\) gives \(E_0[G_bs]=\dot\theta_b(s)\) for unrestricted scores.  Therefore Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}influence\text{-}classes}\), followed by (3)--(4), yields
\[
 \mathcal I_b(P_0)=G_b+\mathcal T_b(P_0)^\perp
 =G_b+\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Finally stack the retained rows in \(R_b\), let \(\Gamma_b=E_0[R_bR_b']\), and let \(u_b=E_0[R_bG_b]\).  The orthogonal projection of \(G_b\) on the finite-dimensional row span is \(R_b'\Gamma_b^\dagger u_b\).  Hence the minimum-norm element of the affine set (5) is
\[
 \phi_b=G_b-R_b'\Gamma_b^\dagger u_b.
 \tag{6}
\]
The Moore--Penrose identities show that (6) is unchanged by redundant displayed rows, completing the proof.
